title: On the Privacy of LLMs: An Ablation Study
abstract: arXiv:2605.02255v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) face diverse privacy threats, yet existing studies typically evaluate individual attacks in isolation, offering limited guidance on which system factors drive privacy vulnerabilities. This paper presents a unified threat model and a systematic ablation study of four representative attacks: Membership Inference (MIA), Attribute Inference (AIA), Data Extraction (DEA), and Backdoor Attacks (BA). Our findings reveal attack-specific sensitivities: membership inference depends strongly on dataset characteristics and attack strategy, attribute inference is influenced by model and training characteristics, data extraction increases with model scale and training-data repetition, and backdoor attacks achieve consistently high success rates. Based on these findings, we derive practical recommendations for privacy-aware LLM deployment, including prioritizing membership leakage assessments in retrieval-augmented

translated_title: 关于大语言模型的隐私性：一项消融研究
translated_abstract: 大语言模型面临多种隐私威胁，然而现有研究通常孤立地评估个别攻击，对于哪些系统因素导致隐私漏洞提供的指导有限。本文提出了一个统一的威胁模型，并对四种代表性攻击进行了系统的消融研究：成员推理攻击（MIA）、属性推理攻击（AIA）、数据提取攻击（DEA）和后门攻击（BA）。我们的发现揭示了针对特定攻击的敏感性：成员推理强烈依赖于数据集特征和攻击策略，属性推理受模型和训练特征的影响，数据提取随模型规模和训练数据重复次数的增加而增加，而后门攻击始终保持较高的成功率。基于这些发现，我们为隐私感知的大语言模型部署提出了实用建议，包括在检索增强场景中优先进行成员泄露评估。
tldr: 本文通过统一的威胁模型对四种代表性隐私攻击进行系统消融研究，揭示了大语言模型隐私漏洞的攻击特异性敏感因素，并为隐私感知的模型部署提供了实用建议。
en_tdlr: This paper presents a unified threat model and a systematic ablation study of four representative privacy attacks on LLMs, revealing attack-specific sensitivity factors and providing practical recommendations for privacy-aware LLM deployment.
